data.rationale: The commit ensures that join alias Vars are flattened in a subquery's targetlist and jointree quals before re-checking for pull-up safety. This is particularly important for LATERAL subqueries because join alias Vars (like a whole-row reference to a join) might hide lateral references that only become visible after flattening. The grammar is extended to allow aliasing join results and using those aliases as whole-row references (e.g., 'ja IS NULL' or 'ja::text') within expressions, which forces the optimizer to handle these join alias Vars during the subquery pull-up process.
seeds: SELECT a1.c0, ss.x FROM t0 AS a1, LATERAL (SELECT (ja IS NULL) AS x FROM (t1 AS a2 LEFT JOIN t2 AS a3 ON false) AS ja) ss;
SELECT a1.c0, a2.c1, ss.y FROM t0 AS a1, t1 AS a2 LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT 1 AS y FROM (t2 AS a3 LEFT JOIN t3 AS a4 ON a3.c0 = a1.c0) AS ja WHERE ja::text IS NOT NULL) ss ON true WHERE a1.c0 = 1;
